newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Juppe says ready to change his ways.
newsitem.headline: France's Juppe says ready to change his ways.

text.p: Unpopular French Prime Minister Alain Juppe said on Monday he was prepared to change his ways if his centre-right government wins a snap parliamentary election.
"To change your ways surely means to renew your team but it also means modernising your methods and your behaviour," Juppe told a campaign rally in the central city of Clermont-Ferrand.
"It means to replace bureaucracy and interventionism with consultation and participation," Juppe said.

Juppe was introduced by former president Valery Giscard d'Estaing, who stung the prime minister's leadership last week by saying he wanted France to shift to bolder and simpler policies and that current President Jacques Chirac should form a new team after the May 27-June 1 election.
The conservative Juppe, highly unpopular in voter surveys, has also come under fire from other members of the majority for lacklustre leadership of the government campaign and unpopular policies.
The criticisms have triggered speculation about possible replacements.
Juppe has so far refused to say whether he wants to keep the job after the election, saying the decision will be up to Chirac. Chirac has also stayed silent on the subject.

Juppe told party loyalists at the Clermont-Ferrand rally that he intended to start putting more emphasis in the campaign on differences between the centre-right and the left and what they would mean for France in the future.
He called the Socialist Party programme "stuck in the past, full of contradictions on Europe, vague and poorly prepared".
